question: Raman's income is ₹43,000. He saves 26% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and 2 expenditure increases by 40%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income = 43000 ⇒ Saving = 26% = 11180 ⇒ Expenditure = 31820

New income = 51600; New expenditure = 44548

New saving = 7052

Decrease in saving = 11180 − 7052 = 4128

**∴ Answer = ₹4128 decrease**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income = ₹43000

Savings = 26% of income

Income increases by 20%

Expenditure increases by 40%

**Formula used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

New value = Old × (1 ± p/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Original saving = 26% of 43000 = 11180

⇒ Original expenditure = 43000 − 11180 = 31820

⇒ New income = 43000 × 1.20 = 51600

⇒ New expenditure = 31820 × 1.40 = 44548

⇒ New saving = 51600 − 44548 = 7052

⇒ Decrease = 11180 − 7052 = 4128

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4128 decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income Relation

Income = Savings + Expenditure

Percentage Change

New value = Old × (1 ± p/100)

Savings Impact

If expenditure increases faster than income, savings decrease

Quick Tip

Always compute new income and expenditure separately before comparing
